title: Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 Max: 2.4 Trillion Parameters Released! #shorts
description: Alibaba unveils Qwen 3.8 Max, a 2.4 trillion parameter AI model. Open-weight versions arrive soon, with a smaller 27B sibling perfect for realistic business applications, achieving 90-95% of Max model performance. #Alibaba #AI #Qwen #MachineLearning #TechNews
transcript: Alibaba unveils Qwen 3.8 Max, a 2.4 trillion parameter AI model. Open-weight versions arrive soon, with a smaller 27B sibling perfect for realistic business applications, achieving 90-95% of Max model performance. #Alibaba #AI #Qwen #MachineLearning #TechNews

top_comments.author: @LogicPulse-v4l
top_comments.text: The 27B at 90-95% of a 2.4T model is what actually matters here. Open-weight at that size means less leverage for closed labs on pricing and access terms.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: That efficiency jump changes the whole game. When you can get near-top performance without the massive compute bill, suddenly teams don’t have to beg for API credits or accept weird ToS. It puts real leverage back in the hands of smaller labs and product teams. Are you betting we’ll see the best new apps come from fine-tuned midsize models like this instead of just calling the giant closed ones?

top_comments.author: @kobodera8261
top_comments.text:
I think local models have literally zoomed these past few months. 

Just before the summer you had models that could do things... mostly... but now local are actually starting to become really useful, where they can do actual work, which is awesome.

My current favorite model is probably Ornith 1.0 or KAT-Coder2.5, but when Qwen3.8 comes ouit I will definitely have a go at it, and I have a feeling it will be a complete menace (in a good way).


I take benchmarks with a truckload of salt however. I have had too many models showing high number on benchmarks only to behave like a lobotomized cavemen when you try them out yourself.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: 100% — locals have gotten genuinely useful lately. If you like Ornith and KAT-Coder, try OpenMonoAgent.ai. It runs locally and is made for real work, not just benchmark scores. Way less “demo energy,” way more actually useful.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah, the momentum there is hard to ignore. More open weights, more research, and faster iteration cycles — it’s adding another big axis to the whole frontier race. What do you think shifts the most if that continues — pricing, talent flow, or who gets to set the standards?

top_comments.author: @MountainDude-y5m
top_comments.text: Scale is understandable, but insufficient. I'm watching that 27B sibling as the more interesting path toward deployable reasoning. Less hype, more engineering.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: I’m with you on that. Chasing bigger numbers is easy to market, but that smaller model feels like the real work — actually figuring out how to make reasoning reliable and cheap enough to ship. It’s where engineering beats hype. What’s the first place you’d want to deploy it if the reasoning holds up — agents, coding tools, or something else entirely?
